subject: Question about legend in stacked histogram

messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Question about legend in stacked histogram
parts:
Dear All,
Please see the snippet at the end of the email.
Everything is fine in this stacked histogram, but as soon as I enable
color="black" in order to have a black line separating the columns of
the histogram, I get a also diagonal line in the legend symbols instead
of simply plain red and blue squares.
Can anyone tell me how to get rid of that line while keeping the figure
as is now?
Best Regards

Lorenzo Isella

######################################################################��


library(ggplot2)

data <- rep(seq(5), 200)
tlab <- rep(c("M","F"),500)


x <- sample(data, 300)

lab <- sample(tlab, 300)

xyz <- cbind(as.data.frame(x),as.data.frame(lab))

names(xyz) <- c("val", "set")
lbls <- levels(xyz$set)
## xyz$val <- levels(xyz$val)[xyz$val]


gpl <- ggplot(xyz, aes(x=val,y=..count.., fill=set, group=set)) +
geom_histogram(alpha=1,
binwidth=1,
origin=0.5,colour="black"
)+
scale_x_continuous()+
opts(legend.text = theme_text(size = 14, vjust=0.4))+
opts(legend.title = theme_text(size = 18,hjust=0))+
opts(legend.position = c(0.45, 0.75),
legend.background=theme_rect(col=0),
legend.key = theme_rect(colour = NA))+


## scale_colour_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values="black") +
scale_fill_manual("", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c("blue","red"))+


opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(axis.ticks = theme_segment(colour = "black", size=1),
axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"))+
xlab("Answer")+
ylab("Number of people")+

## scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,20, by=1))+

opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
# opts(title = expression(paste("Dublin")))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(plot.title = theme_text(size = 25))+
## opts(plot.title = theme_blank())+
## opts(title = expression(paste("SG+elsewhere")))+


opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="black", hjust=1))

postscript("test.eps", width=5,height=5,horizontal = FALSE,
onefile = FALSE, paper = "special"## ,
## family = "ComputerModern", encoding = "TeXtext.enc"
)
print(gpl)
dev.off()
